subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint: performance benchmarking review and next tuning steps
messages:
From: Sam Reed <sam.reed@acmehealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 7 May 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint — perf numbers + asks

Hi Karthik / Grace,

Thanks for the call earlier. Per our MAP timeline I wanted to share the perf snapshot from our staging runs and flag a couple of items we'd like prioritized for the close timeline. Attachment: acme_weekly_bench_q2.csv (summary below).

Quick highlights from the CSV:
- Median p50 latency (prompt+gen) on 8k token corp: 185 ms
- 95th percentile latency: 620 ms
- Sustained throughput (tokens/s) with batch=8: 9.4k ts
- Cold-start tail noted on infrequent API keys (spike to ~1.5s)

Key asks for this week (aligned to MAP dates):
1) Reduce 95th percentile to <500 ms for 8k token workload or document fallback behavior.
2) Investigate cold-start spike and propose short-term mitigations (warm pool / faster routing).
3) Quick quantization trial (int8) on a dev node to validate quality delta by EOW.

We have the mutual action plan milestone of vendor acceptance on May 16; the above items are blockers for our final sign-off. Can you confirm owners and ETA for each? Happy to join a quick session if you want a live look at the runs.

Thanks,
Sam
Sam Reed
Head of Platform Eng, AcmeHealth

Sam — thanks for this and for the clear asks. Forwarding the CSV into our MAP tracker and calling out owners below.

Brief plan / owners (ETA column):
- 95th percentile reduction: Rishi to lead latency primer (kernel selection, batching tweaks). ETA: May 13 (profiling complete), May 15 (playbook w/ rollback).
- Cold-start spikes: Neha to prototype a warm-pool + lightweight health-check routing rule for infrequently used keys. ETA: May 12 for a PoC; May 14 for a runbook.
- Int8 quant trial: Grace to run quantized dev instance (compare decoding quality on the provided eval set). ETA: May 9 EOD for initial quality delta report.

Action items (owners):
- Rishi: full p95 profile, include model kernel/cudnn versions and per-step breakdown. (Rishi)
- Neha: warm-pool config and synthetic replay test for cold-key spikes. (Neha)
- Grace: quant trial artifacts + brief evaluation (BLEU/ROUGE-ish checks we use). (Grace)
- Karthik: collate MAP slide with decision criteria for May 14 review and raise any SLA exception requests. (Karthik)

Sam — we'll send a short status update in the MAP tracker by EOD Fri and propose a 30-min sync early next week if needed.

- Karthik

Thanks Karthik — that owner breakdown works for us. A couple clarifying notes from our side:

- For the p95 target: if you cannot hit <500 ms at scale, please include a documented graceful degradation path (e.g., route to a slightly lower-cost model variant with identical API but flagged in response metadata).
- For quant: quality regression tolerance we set at "no more than 1.5% end-to-end metric delta" on our eval set — if the int8 trial exceeds that, we'll want to see a fallback.

Also looping in our procurement timeline: we need final SLA language by May 15 to present to legal on May 16. If your May 15 internal playbook isn't available, flag immediately so we can expand the acceptance window.

Appreciate the quick turn.

— Elena
Procurement Manager, AcmeHealth

Quick internal follow-up after the handoff — locking in owners and immediate next steps:

1) Rishi: start the p95 profile (I gave you the CSV + eval set link). Deliverable: profiling doc + preliminary tuning knobs by 2025-05-13.
2) Neha: spin the warm-pool PoC on a single dev cluster; include a simple synthetic load test to reproduce the spike. Deliverable: PoC notes + runbook draft by 2025-05-12.
3) Grace: quant run on dev instance, capture quality/latency tradeoff, include output artifacts in MAP-v1.3.pdf. Deliverable: quant report + examples by 2025-05-09 EOD.
4) Karthik: prepare the May 14 MAP decision slide and draft SLA exception request if >500ms p95 persists. Deliverable: slide deck + exception doc by 2025-05-14.

I've added these action items to MAP-4521 and shared the Drive link (see related_links). I'll ping Sam/Elena after we have the first artifacts. If anyone is blocked, call out blockers in the Jira ticket — avoid last-minute surprises for procurement.

Thanks team,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Engineering, Redwood Inference
